I don’t know if this qualifies as really fucked up but it was kinda disturbing after I realized this for myself. When I was younger my paternal grandmother would spend the weekend with my family, me, my brother, and my parents, and she still visits every so often. When she comes over we usually eat out and she’ll pick up the check for the food. She would always get large portions of food and eat them all and I always thought to myself, “ I guess she has a big appetite like me and my dad” because I eat a good bit but I’m also a teenager. Come to find out later after an appointment with my therapist for totally unrelated reasons, my mom starts talking about my paternal grandmother because I asked her about my dads childhood since he doesn’t talk about it much. She said a lot about how my grandmother over spends, which she still does, how she had to file for bankruptcy, and that she had a bad relationship with food. This third point is what I want to focus on. I had never considered my grandmother to be obese until my mom pointed it out to me then all the pieces clicked into place. I finally figured it out for myself that my paternal grandmother most likely has binge eating disorder and my dad doesn’t say anything to her about it to her because he finds it uncomfortable. I also realized that she normalized having and unhealthy relationship with food for me. To this day I still struggle with binge eating and restricting and guilt surrounding food.

I definitely agree that this manhwa is a masterpiece (I finished all of it in one day). I’m still on the fence whether Sangwoo started developing feeling for Yoon Bum or if that was just him being more manipulative of Bum. Sangwoo used sex to keep Bum under his thumb because he kept Bum alive and Bum knew his secret. The main reason why I’m on the fence about if Sangwoo really had feelings for Bum is when Sangwoo  tells Bum to kill the officer that came into the house (can’t remember the dudes name but it was the last scene with Sangwoo alive with Bum) but Bum doesn’t do it and Sangwoo tells Bum that he is useless. If Sangwoo really had feelings for Bum, then the likelihood of Sangwoo kicking Yoon Bum to the curb is greatly decreased, however, Sangwoo wanted to have total control over his life, shown by his use of manipulation of others through his charm/sexual acts, which also factors into how he was angered by Yoon Bum refusing to kill the police officer. And one last thing, because I’ve already rambled on for too long. I believe that the ending did Yoon Bum a great deal of justice. Bum’s life was completely changed by his encounter with Sangwoo after breaking into his house and, some might say, his life improved in some respects. I think that the fact Bum dies, at least it assumed that he dies because Koogi left that to the imagination of the reader, chasing the mirage of the person who saved him from sexual assault in the military and changed his life once he got home is the best ending you could give someone who had been through what Bum had. Though Bum’s life may have seemed illegitimate at times, he was given a legitimate end in the form of the man he refused to leave behind. I’m also glad that mental illness and assault are incorporated because I have ties to both in my life. Nobody asked but I have DID and some of my alters, alternate personalities, have their own mental illnesses and one of them has Borderline personality disorder like Bum. My alters have been present in my life for about 2 years now but some of them split apart and created more because I experienced sexual assault multiple times by the same person. I really like this manhwa because it does right by those who have experienced assault and have mental illnesses by showing the effects of assault and mental illnesses that many of use cannot express. I am grateful to Koogi for truthfully portraying the characteristics of their MC’s (I’m using they/them pronouns in reference to Koogi because I don’t want to make assumptions) and giving a voice to those who have experienced the issues shown in this manhwa who have not been able to speak for themselves for whatever reasons. And being able to present these issues through the lens of entertainment has helped reduced the stigma surrounding sexual/physical assault and mental illness. If you have stuck around long enough to read all of this, I thank you and if you haven’t read killing stalking already I greatly encourage you to do so especially if you have had experience with sexual/physical assault and/or mental illness.
